subject: Optikon dedicated capacity — slot sizing, surge buffer & preemption policy
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Optikon sizing request and conflict with existing reserved lanes

Avery —

Fwd-ing Optikon's sizing ask and the quick sketch of their SOW. They want a baseline of 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved 24/7 for production, with burst to 12 for peak inference windows. Optikon is asking for a "no-preempt" SLA for baseline capacity.

Problem: the pool they target (us-west-2b-pool-3) is currently at 92% committed across existing reserved deals and our soft-preempt policies; if we allocate 8 full guaranteed GPUs for them we will need to either:
- reassign lower-priority commitments (affects other enterprise customers), or
- carve a new pool (lead time ~2–3 weeks, scheduling ops/infra), or
- allow burst from the shared burst pool with preemption.

Can you advise on commercial flexibility here? Optikon is on a tight timeline — they want a firm start by June 10. I included their sizing doc and a draft SOW.

Attachments: Optikon_SizingRequest_v2.pdf (Attachment), Optikon_SOW_draft.docx (Attachment)

Thanks,
Karthik
---
Karthik Iyer
Director, Revenue Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Optikon sizing request and conflict with existing reserved lanes

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick brief. High-level thoughts:

1) Commercial compromise: offer a guaranteed baseline of 4 reserved GPUs + burst access to 4 GPUs from the shared pool. Burst to 8 guaranteed only on a 12-month commit. We can price the burst at a premium (e.g., 1.6x) and include a 12-hour preemption notice SLA.

2) Technical mitigation: reduce per-token footprint by recommending 4-bit quant profiles and aggressive KV caching for their steady-state flows; that could reduce the effective GPU footprint by ~20%. Ask Product to produce a suggested quant/profile.

3) Operational runway: Monica, can your procurement team draft a redline that reflects the tiered guarantee (baseline 4 + burst 4) and the escalation clause for increasing to 8 after the commitment term?

If Ops can provision a soft-dedicated lane in a neighboring AZ (us-west-2c) and delay start by 2 weeks, that may also be acceptable to Optikon. Let's sync for 30m this afternoon — dropping a Zoom link.

Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Manager, Dedicated Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Capacity impact analysis (Optikon request)

Avery / Karthik —

I ran a quick impact model on the us-west-2b pool. Key takeaways attached (fleet-utilization-weekly.csv, priority-impact-matrix.xlsx). Short summary:

- Full 8-GPU guaranteed for Optikon starting June 10 results in a 9.4% increase in 95th-percentile latency for two existing enterprise customers (our high-throughput accounts) during daily peak windows.
- Soft-preempt (gradual shedding of burst instances with 12hr notice) limits customer impact to <2% at 95th pct.
- Creating a separate dedicated lane in us-west-2c requires ~14 business days of infra scheduling and an Ops window that pushes start to June 24.

Proposals (ordered by risk):
A) Baseline 4 guaranteed + burst 4 with 12hr preemption notice + 1-week production canary. (Lowest immediate operational risk; keeps latency impact minimal.)
B) 8 guaranteed but only if Optikon signs 12-month committed contract and pays a surcharge to backfill risk (we'd need a 20% margin uplift).
C) Delay start and provision a new isolated lane in us-west-2c (best isolation, slower delivery).

I recommend A for now so we can meet the customer's timeline and preserve performance for others. If leadership prefers B, include the margin uplift and an SLA addendum for preemption exceptions.

(Attachment: fleet-utilization-weekly.csv, priority-impact-matrix.xlsx)

-Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Capacity Planning — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@optikon.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Optikon sizing request and conflict with existing reserved lanes

Hi Avery / Karthik —

Thank you for the analysis. Optikon's product launch cannot tolerate baseline preemption — our enterprise customers require stable 8x GPUs for the first 90 days of production. We are willing to sign a 12-month commit if you can confirm firm baseline 8 GPUs with a 99.5% availability SLA (no preemption) and a 10% annual price reduction for that term.

If that is not possible, please propose a short-term bridge (30-day guaranteed baseline) and a technical plan to avoid live-customer regressions. We need final confirmation by Friday, June 2 to proceed with our launch plan.

Regards,
Elena Suarez
Head of Infrastructure — Optikon Systems
(Attachment: commercial-term-sheet.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 May 2028 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Optikon sizing request and conflict with existing reserved lanes

Looping me in for exec decisioning. Two asks for leadership:
1) Margin calc: if we provide 8 guaranteed for 12 months, what is net margin after we account for potential SLA credits and the opportunity cost of shifting or preempting other customers? Naomi — can you put numbers to that?
2) Runbook: if we do baseline 4 + burst 4 with preemption notice, what's the customer-facing runbook and how do we guarantee the 12hr notice? Laura, can you draft a short E2E runbook and the Ops steps to turn burst on/off?

We need both answers before committing to B. If the numbers look favorable, I can approve a one-off executive exception to reserve a new lane.

-Ben
Ben Carter
VP, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Decision & next steps — Optikon provisioning (proposed)

Team — finalizing plan based on timeline and risk tolerance. Proposed decision:

- Provision baseline: 4 reserved GPUs in us-west-2b-pool-3 immediately (target provisioning window: June 6–8).
- Burst: grant access to up to 4 additional GPUs from the shared burst pool, subject to a 12-hour preemption notice. Burst will be priced at 1.6x baseline rate.
- Commercial: offer a convertible commitment: if Optikon signs a 12-month firm commit by June 30, convert to 8 guaranteed GPUs with a 10% committed discount; otherwise the baseline remains 4 and bursts remain preemptible.
- Canary: run a 7-day production canary starting on provisioning with SLA monitoring dashboards and a "rollback" preplan.
- Exec ask: Ben, request that you sign-off on the convertible commitment terms and the margin runway; Laura, draft the customer-facing runbook and the Ops procedure for 12hr preemption and the canary test plan. Monica, prepare the redline for procurement.

I'll reply to Optikon with this proposal and the June 2 confirmation deadline in their timezone. If we get their acceptance and they commit to the convertible term, we'll schedule the full lane migration and revise pricing.

Avery Johnson
Senior Manager, Dedicated Accounts — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: decision-summary.txt)
